examInfo.subject: 英文
examInfo.group: 大學組第一、二、三、四類組
examInfo.title: 114學年度身心障礙學生升學大專校院甄試 英文

questions.text: The victory in the 2024 international baseball game does not represent the success of one individual but rather a ______ effort of the whole team.
steps: 「joint effort」意為「共同努力」，符合「整個團隊的努力」的語境。

questions.text: You should ______ this button back on your shirt right away before you lose it.
steps: 「sew a button」（縫鈕釦）是固定搭配，指把鈕釦縫回衣服上。

questions.text: You should come to the party tonight; it is a good chance to ______ with colleagues from other departments.
steps: 「network with someone」意為「與人建立人脈、交流拓展關係」，符合與其他部門同事互動的語境。

questions.text: The employee solved the problem, but her boss took all the ______ instead.
steps: 「take credit」意為「把功勞攬為己有」，符合上司搶走部屬功勞的語境。

questions.text: Customers are required by the restaurant to pay a ______ of NT$1,000 when they make the reservation.
steps: 「deposit」意為「訂金、押金」，符合訂位時須先支付一筆款項的語境。

questions.text: The mayor’s phone has been ringing ______ since the news about the scandal was released this morning.
steps: 「ringing constantly」意為「持續不斷地響」，符合電話從早上開始不停響的語境。

questions.text: The survivors were in ______ need of medical help as many of them had been seriously injured in the air crash.
steps: 「urgent need」意為「急迫的需求」，符合空難重傷倖存者急需醫療協助的語境。

questions.text: The host of the talk show has received many complaints from the audience as one of the guest speakers made some really ______ statements in the show.
steps: 「objectionable」意為「令人反感、招致反對的」，符合來賓發言引起觀眾大量投訴抱怨的語境。

questions.text: Please put that ______ of books in the recycle bin after you clean off the shelf.
steps: 「a stack of books」意為「一疊書」，是常見搭配用語。

questions.text: The missing child’s family is desperately seeking any possible information about his activities or ______.
steps: 「whereabouts」意為「下落、行蹤」，符合家屬急欲得知失蹤孩童行蹤的語境。

questions.text: （空格 11）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「Owing to」意為「由於、因為」，表因果關係，符合「因空氣濕度不足，故經歷乾燥氣候」的語意邏輯。

questions.text: （空格 12）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「cope with」意為「應付、因應」，符合動物演化出適應機制以「應付」低溫的語境。

questions.text: （空格 13）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 此處為過去分詞作後位修飾語（省略關係代名詞及be動詞的化簡關係子句），意即「被發現於戈壁沙漠的雙峰駱駝」，故用過去分詞found。

questions.text: （空格 14）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「accumulation and melting」（積雪與融雪）是一組相對的自然過程，兩者共同劇烈改變地貌景觀，語意通順。

questions.text: （空格 15）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「surroundings」意為「周遭環境」，符合動物改變體色以配合環境變化、避免被天敵發現的語境。

questions.text: （空格 16）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「flood into」意為「湧入」，符合大批購物者湧入實體店面搶購優惠的語境。

questions.text: （空格 17）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「使用……來描述……」為不定詞表目的的用法：begin using X to describe Y，故填不定詞to describe。

questions.text: （空格 18）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 「work longer shifts」意為「輪值更長的班次」，符合警察因應人潮需超時輪班工作的語境。

questions.text: （空格 19）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 前段是警方角度的命名由來解釋，此處以「However」（然而）轉折，引出另一種從會計角度出發的不同解釋。

questions.text: （空格 20）請選出最適當的選項。
steps: 此句與前半部「red ink indicated a loss」為對稱平行結構，「demonstrated」（顯示、表明）與「indicated」意義相近，符合對稱語意「黑色墨水則顯示獲利」。

questions.text: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: The invasion of snakes has caused the ecosystem of Guam to be out of balance.
options.B: The birds on Guam are dying out because of the introduction of snakes.
options.C: The population of spiders is exploding on Guam due to the absence of birds.
options.D: The unpredictable weather system has turned Guam into a hellish island.

steps: 全文涵蓋蛇入侵導致鳥類滅絕、進而造成蜘蛛數量暴增等一連串生態連鎖反應，主旨應是「蛇的入侵造成關島生態系失衡」這個較全面的概念，(A)最為適當，其餘選項僅涵蓋文章的部分內容（單獨鳥類滅絕或蜘蛛暴增），並非完整主旨；(D)則與文章內容（生態入侵，非天氣）無關。
questions.final: 答案：(A) The invasion of snakes has caused the ecosystem of Guam to be out of balance.

questions.text: What does one in Paragraph Two refer to?
steps: 第二段提及蛇「emptying the jungle of every single one」，呼應第一段提到的原生鳥類（native birds），且後文接著說「12種鳥類中10種已滅絕」，故「one」指的是「鳥（bird）」。

questions.text: Which of the following is closest in meaning to “Guam’s spider population may once have been unremarkable” in Paragraph Four?

options.A: There may have been few spiders on Guam before.
options.B: The spider’s webs on Guam were not remarkably beautiful before.
options.C: The number of spiders used to be smaller than the population of Guam.
options.D: There may have been more spiders on Guam than on the nearby islands.

steps: 「unremarkable」意為「不特別顯眼、不出眾」，套用於蜘蛛族群數量，意指當時蜘蛛數量並不特別多、不引人注目，最接近選項(A)「以前可能蜘蛛數量很少」的說法。
questions.final: 答案：(A) There may have been few spiders on Guam before.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely the major organizational structure of the passage?
steps: 全文以「蛇的入侵」為起因，依序說明其導致鳥類滅絕、蜘蛛暴增等一連串「結果」，屬於典型的「因果關係」（cause-effect）文章組織架構。

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Wildlife scientists managed to correct the mistakes made by human.
options.B: Guam has 40 times more spiders than neighboring islands all year round.
options.C: Brown tree snakes were intentionally imported into Guam by merchants.
options.D: In the Bahamas, there are more spiders on islands without lizards.

steps: 文中明確提及巴哈馬的研究發現「沒有蜥蜴（其天敵）的島嶼上蜘蛛數量約多10倍」，符合(D)敘述。(A)錯誤：文末說明「入侵者正在獲勝」，人類尚未成功糾正此生態問題。(B)錯誤：文中限定「雨季期間」蜘蛛數量為鄰近島嶼的40倍，並非「全年」皆是如此。(C)錯誤：文中說明棕樹蛇是「意外（accidentally）」隨貨船引入，並非商人「刻意」引進。
questions.final: 答案：(D) In the Bahamas, there are more spiders on islands without lizards.

p11_15.title: 11-15 題組
p11_15.html:
Most of the time, when we hear the word “desert,” we picture vast stretches of sand, hot dry winds, and scorching heat. But do you know that not all deserts are hot? Cold deserts, also known as “temperate deserts,” have cold temperatures all year long. Usually, they are located in interior areas far from the coast or near high mountains with low humidity.　＿＿(11)＿＿ the lack of air moisture, they experience dry weather and very little rain or snow.
Most animals living in cold deserts have developed adaptations to　＿＿(12)＿＿ the falling temperatures. These adaptions may be in the form of thick fur, scaly skin, or the ability to store water in their bodies. For example, Bactrian camels　＿＿(13)＿＿ in the Gobi desert have thick and hairy coats to keep them warm during the cold winters. They shed these thick coats as summer sets in.
The accumulation and ＿＿(14)＿＿ of snow changes the landscapes of cold deserts drastically. Many cold desert animals change their color to match their changing ＿＿(15)＿＿ so as to protect themselves from being seen and preyed upon. For instance, ptarmigan birds have brownish feathers during the warm summers when the landscape is brown and muddy, and they molt into white feathers during winter months when the ground is covered in snow.

p16_20.title: 16-20 題組
p16_20.html:
The day following Thanksgiving—commonly known as Black Friday—has become one of the busiest shopping days of the year in the United States. Every year, millions of shoppers visit websites and ＿＿(16)＿＿ stores on that day, seeking the best deals of the season. But how did this shopping tradition come to be called “Black Friday”?
An explanation dates back to the early 1960s, when police officers in Philadelphia began using “Black Friday”　＿＿(17)＿＿ the disorder that resulted on that day when large numbers of suburban tourists came into the city for their Christmas shopping and attended an important annual sports event on Saturday. The huge crowds created a headache for the police, who worked longer　＿＿(18)＿＿　than usual as they dealt with traffic jams, accidents, shoplifting, and other problems.
＿＿(19)＿＿ , many look at this name through an accounting lens. Back when accounting records were kept by hand, red ink indicated a loss and black　＿＿(20)＿＿ a profit. As businessmen began to realize they could draw big crowds by discounting prices, Black Friday was described as the day stores began to turn a profit for the year. Over time, the name evolved, taking on an entirely new meaning tied to the success of the retailing business nationwide.

p21_25.title: 21-25 題組
p21_25.html:
On the island of Guam in the western Pacific Ocean, a party was interrupted by an uninvited guest: a brown form curled around the remaining roast pig, swallowing the pig’s flesh whole. The visitor was a brown tree snake, an alien invader which is thought to have been accidentally introduced to Guam in the 1940s, perhaps after sneaking onto a cargo ship.
Before this, an abundance of native birds had enjoyed their life in the island’s otherworldly forests. But within just four decades of the snake’s invasion, these predators had begun emptying the jungle of every single one. Out of 12 species, ten are now extinct on the island. Without birds to disperse seeds, trees are dying out, and the ecosystem is changing.
What’s scarier is that an evolutionary experiment is unfolding. On most of the Mariana Islands in the Pacific Ocean, there are relatively few spiders in the rainy season, with a large increase in number as the climate dries out. But not on Guam. There is a near-continuous tangle of silvery threads of webs that stretches for miles, going from ground level all the way up to the treetops, all year round.
To find out how many spiders had taken over Guam, some scientists set about doing surveys in the island’s forests. The scientists found that during the wet season, there were 40 times more spiders in Guam’s forests than on the nearby islands of Rota, Tinian, and Saipan. Since Rota, Tinian, and Saipan are free of brown tree snakes and still have healthy bird populations, the study suggests that Guam’s spider population may once have been unremarkable, before the absence of birds. And it fits with research conducted in the Bahamas, which has found that spiders are about 10 times more abundant on islands where there are no lizards—their natural enemy.
Though conservationists and wildlife officials have used every conceivable method, like using viruses as bioweapons or toxic poisons, to eliminate the brown tree snakes from Guam, the invaders are winning.
